root.name: Scandinavian Defense: Marshall Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. d4 Nxd5

overview: Black has regained the d5 pawn with the knight, avoiding the tempo loss of an early queen. White gets a space edge with 4.Nf3 or 4.c4 Nb6, and Black develops with ...g6 and ...Bg7 or ...Bf5, ...e6 and ...c6. Black's position is a bit cramped but sound and easy to play; White tries to use the extra space with Nc3, Bd3 and a kingside castle.

white_ideas.idea: 4.c4 Nb6 to gain space and attack the knight, with Nc3 and Be3
Nf3, Be2 and O-O, simply developing with a small space edge
Exploit the lead in space to attack d5/b6 or kingside

black_ideas.idea: Develop with ...g6/...Bg7 or ...Bf5 and ...e6, castle and aim for ...c5
Hit the centre with ...c5 or ...e5 to free the position
Aim for a safe, harmonious position and gradually equalise

typical_structures.structure: White d4/c4 space against Black ...Nb6/...e6/...c6, Caro-like structures

character.notes: Black gets a sound but slightly cramped position with easy development; few early tactics, so steady.

structure.notes: Asymmetric centre with White pawn on d4 and half-open d-file; Scandinavian is Semi-open per the rubric.

approach.notes: A recognised reply to 1.e4, less common than main defences but played at every level, so standard.

sublines_that_differ.name: 4.c4 Nb6
sublines_that_differ.how: White gets a big space edge and Black hunts for ...c5 or ...e6 counterplay.

character.reason: Black's position is sound, if cramped, with few quick ways to lose.

gambit.reason: Black regains the pawn at once.

structure.reason: Asymmetric centre with a half-open d-file for Black.

approach.reason: Less common than main lines but respectable at every level.

level.reason: Plans are clear and theory is modest.

plans.reason: White gets space and Black has to find room for its pieces.
